solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dirty spots in part of plane, craft beset by bacteria

parts.note: a fin is the tail part of an aeroplane

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so the craft sits inside the bacteria

parts.note: germs are bacteria in everyday speech
Noah's ark is the classic crossword craft

explanation.surface: A grubby aeroplane interior, its surfaces crawling with bacteria.
explanation.definitionFit: Smudges left by grubby hands on glass or paper are the dirty spots meant here.

clue.text: One unenthralled following about upset celebrity

parts.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, something upset is turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Someone liberated who cares nothing for a fallen star.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral originally meant to enslave, so someone never enslaved is a citizen with full liberty, not a serf.

clue.text: Annoy rest after leader's changed direction

indicators.note: the leading letter is a compass point, south, and it is changed to the opposite direction, north

parts.note: to settle is to come to rest

explanation.surface: Someone at peace is irritated once the boss changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's changed direction' swaps the S that starts SETTLE for N.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate them, like the sting of the plant.

clue.text: Festival dislikes including Queen covers

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so the monarch goes inside the pair of words

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival
to have a down on someone is to dislike them, so downs are dislikes
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual queen

explanation.surface: A queen with grumbles about a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Quilts stuffed with duck feathers are bedspreads, which are covers for a bed.

clue.text: Woman for all to see filling potty

indicators.note: something filling another sits inside it, so the film rating goes in the middle

parts.note: potty is British slang for crazy
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A woman on display for everyone while sitting on a child's potty.
explanation.definitionFit: Maud is a female first name, as in Tennyson's poem, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Access content of free channel

indicators.note: the content of something is what lies inside it, so only the inner letters count

parts.note: the two inside letters of the word
a course is a channel, as of a river

explanation.surface: Getting to watch a free television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Having recourse to something means having a source of help available to use, so it is access to it.

clue.text: Altercation oddly is all about environment

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the first, third and fifth positions

parts.note: odd letters of the two words read together

explanation.surface: A row that is all about the environment, as eco-campaigners argue.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to space or surroundings, so a word about one's environment.

clue.text: Warned of alcoholic drink, wine containing Tango

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside, so the wine wraps round the letter

parts.note: red is wine
Tango is T in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone cautioned about drink after a bottle of wine at a tango evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put on guard or made aware of danger is to be cautioned, the same as being warned.

clue.text: Car a rock clipped with damage on metal

indicators.note: clipped means the word has its tail cut off

parts.note: a stone is a piece of rock
to mar is to damage or spoil
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A vehicle bodywork is chipped by a stone and dented.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Martin is a British maker of luxury sports cars, so its name stands for one of them.

clue.text: Open shed damaged here from leprechaun's larking

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so these letters are removed from the fodder
damaged signals the letters of here may come out in any order from the pool
larking means fooling about, so the letters of the fodder are played with and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, every letter including the s
the letters to be taken out

explanation.surface: A mischievous leprechaun breaks open a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden hut opened by the leprechaun but it is the verb: HERE is cast off from LEPRECHAUNS and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclasp something is to release its catch, so to open it.

clue.text: Mean sorts keeping silence regularly for entertaining acts

parts.note: par is the average or mean

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the selected letters are held inside

parts.note: types are sorts or kinds

indicators.note: regularly takes letters at a fixed interval, here every other one starting from the second

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Stingy people staying quiet through the after-dinner entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean sorts' reads as misers, but it splits into the average and kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is a song or trick someone habitually performs to amuse guests, so an entertaining act.

clue.text: Locks might contain these vessels

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the pivoting parts inside a lock that a key must line up

explanation.surface: Canal locks holding boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks and vessels suggest a canal with boats in it; the locks are door locks and the vessels are glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the levers in a lock mechanism and straight-sided drinking glasses.

clue.text: Auditor's appointed by assistant

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are taken as heard

parts.note: appointed means due, as at an appointed time, and by means near

explanation.surface: An accountant reporting who appointed the assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant; here it is just a hearer. In southern British speech 'due' is said 'joo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior is a subordinate who works under someone senior, so an assistant.

clue.text: Successfully finished in TT?

parts.note: surface reading: winning a TT motorbike race on the Isle of Man; setter's reading: TT also stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from drink, and a finished racer is past the line

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means safely finished, and its second half also describes a teetotaller, so TT is both the race and the abstainer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having safely completed something with success assured, like a horse past the winning post.

clue.text: Pens around this figure? You'd find a range

definitions.meaning: surface reading: animal enclosures built round a shape
setter's reading: put the word pens round a number and you get the hills forming England's backbone, between Derbyshire and the Scottish border

explanation.walkthrough: Pens wrapped round the number gives PEN-NINE-S, the Pennines, a range of hills in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a number, and a number is a figure; the cryptic part finds it by its place inside the range's name.

clue.text: Company partner occupied by deficit hugely

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has that thing inside it

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
an ally is a partner
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A business partner swamped by enormous debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The deficit goes between the company and the partner, as if inside the combined pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a giant statue, so doing something colossally means on a gigantic scale.

clue.text: Roll and roll around beginning to remedy skin inflammation

parts.note: to wind is to roll up, as with a ball of yarn

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the bread surrounds the chosen letter

parts.note: a bun is a bread roll

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: Rolling a bread roll around while looking for a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'roll' changes sense: first a verb, then a piece of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure to strong wind leaves skin red and sore, an irritation like sunburn.

clue.text: Our tea ordered with nice salesperson

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ordering tea from a pleasant shop assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a sale by taking bids is a kind of seller, a person selling goods.

clue.text: Do show contempt for losing first argument

indicators.note: losing first means the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: to scorn is to show contempt for
a row is an argument

explanation.surface: Someone disdains an argument they are losing at the first stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the noun, a hairdo, not the verb it looks like. SCORN without its S gives CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornrow is a hairstyle of tight braids lying flat on the scalp, an example of a hairdo.

clue.text: Greek character going back in swimmer's headwear

indicators.note: the Greek letter pi at the front of the word moves back to the end, still within the word

parts.note: a pike is a freshwater fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A letter from the Greek alphabet is returned inside a bather's cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character going back in' moves the PI at the front of PIKE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat round top and a peak.

clue.text: Harsh part of text remembered

indicators.note: part of says only a portion of the words that follow is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A cruel passage of writing that sticks in the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe measures go to the furthest degree, so harsh treatment is described as drastic in this sense.

clue.text: Aluminium lid over a source of fibre

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: a cap is a lid
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aluminium lid placed over a container, as if describing kitchenware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of fibre' sounds dietary, like bran; it is wool.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American animal is sheared for its soft wool, which is spun into yarn, a textile fibre.

clue.text: Rant hearing attack from Asian person?

indicators.note: hearing means what follows is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a raid is an attack, and a Thai is a person from Thailand

explanation.surface: A furious outburst on learning of an assault by someone from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of denunciation is a harangue, which is exactly what a rant is.

clue.text: Examining an urban settlement in California to the west

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftwards, so the words travel right to left

parts.note: a city is a large urban settlement
LA, Los Angeles, is the big city in California

explanation.surface: An investigation into a town on the western side of California.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the city and LA are turned; 'an' stays as it is at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An analytic approach breaks a thing down to study it closely, so it describes the act of examining.

clue.text: Chamber orchestra players half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut, usually meaning tipsy, here says half the word is chopped away

parts.note: string players found in an orchestra; the second half goes

explanation.surface: Members of a chamber orchestra who are a little drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber orchestra' reads as a phrase, but the definition is 'Chamber' alone; half-cut is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery, and a room is a chamber.

clue.text: Training time, jog back alongside river

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to jog is to run slowly
t is the abbreviation for time
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A training session spent jogging back along a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurture is the upbringing and education given to a child, so it is a form of training.

clue.text: Underwear designers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: knickers or long underpants
second meaning: people who draw, sketching plans

explanation.surface: Fashion people who design lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests lingerie designers; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for knickers and also, read literally, people who sketch and draft.

clue.text: Retired woman tucked into fish and green cheese

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the whole string is read backwards
something tucked into another is placed inside it

parts.note: eels are fish
a lady is a woman
green means inexperienced or new

explanation.surface: A retired lady eating fish with green vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' sits at the front but governs the whole assembled string, not just the woman; green meaning new is the inexperienced sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Wensleydale is a crumbly white cheese from a Yorkshire valley, favoured by Wallace and Gromit.
